706	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
707	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
708	// plain-text 404.
709	//
710	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
711	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
712	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
713	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
714	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
715	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
716		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
717			p := r.URL.Path
718	
719			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
720			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
721			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
722				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
723			}
724	
725			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedDocumentDelete(r.Method, p) || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) || malformedPermissionPath(p) || malformedChangeExportPath(p) || malformedChangeQueryPath(p) || malformedSessionChangesPath(p) || malformedSessionPollPath(p) || malformedSessionReplayPath(p) || malformedSessionMergePath(p) || malformedSessionCompactPath(p) || malformedSessionQueryPath(p) || malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p) || malformedSessionRestorePath(p) {
726				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
727				return
728			}
729			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
730		})
731	}

733	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
734	// long-poll/replay/merge/restore/compaction endpoints but is not that
735	// endpoint's exact location: a missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra
736	// segments, or a "poll"/"replay"/"merge"/"restore"/"compact" segment in a
737	// position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
738	// 301 redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the new endpoints promise a JSON error
739	// and never a redirect, so every such path is a malformed 400.
740	//
741	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
742	// happen to be named "poll", "replay", "merge", "restore" or "compact" keep
743	// their ordinary merge/snapshot/changes routes.
744	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
745		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
746		if !ok {
747			return false
748		}
749		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
750	
751		// The named-snapshot-version subtree ({documentID}/snapshots/versions/...)
752		// owns its whole shape verdict through malformedSnapshotPath. A version
753		// name may coincide with a change keyword ("poll", "merge", "restore",
754		// "subscribe", "compact"), so none of the keyword loops below may judge a
755		// path inside that subtree; leave it to the snapshot guard.
756		if len(segs) >= 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "snapshots" && segs[2] == "versions" {
757			return false
758		}
759	
760		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
761		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
762		for i, seg := range segs {
763			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
764				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
765			}
766		}
767		// Document change subscription: "subscribe" must be exactly the third
768		// segment, after a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace
769		// has its own state/subscribe endpoint and its own guard, so a "subscribe"
770		// under crdt/ is not the change-subscription keyword.
771		for i, seg := range segs {
772			if seg == "subscribe" && i > 0 {
773				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
774					continue
775				}
776				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
777			}
778		}
779		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
780		// non-empty documentID.
781		for i, seg := range segs {
782			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
783				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
784			}
785		}
786		// Merge and restore endpoints: each keyword must be exactly the second
787		// segment, after a non-empty documentID (they are document-item
788		// subresources, unlike poll/compact which sit below the change
789		// collection). A keyword used as a version name inside the versions
790		// subtree was excluded by the early return above.
791		for _, keyword := range []string{"merge", "restore"} {
792			for i, seg := range segs {
793				if seg == keyword && i > 0 {
794					return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
795				}
796			}
797		}
798		// Compaction endpoint: "compact" must be exactly the third segment, after
799		// a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace has its own
800		// guard; "compact" there is the CRDT compaction keyword, not the
801		// change-log one.
802		for i, seg := range segs {
803			if seg == "compact" && i > 0 {
804				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
805					return false
806				}
807				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
808			}
809		}
810		return false
811	}

813	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
814	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
815	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
816	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
817	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
818	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
819	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
820	//
821	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
822	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
823	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
824	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
825	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
826	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
827		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
828		if !ok {
829			return false
830		}
831		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
832		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
833		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
834		// keyword.
835		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
836			return false
837		}
838		// The named-snapshot-version subtree owns its whole shape verdict; a
839		// version name coinciding with "subscribe" is an ordinary identifier
840		// there, not the change-subscription keyword.
841		if inSessionSnapshotVersionsSubtree(segs) {
842			return false
843		}
844		for i, seg := range segs {
845			if seg != "subscribe" {
846				continue
847			}
848			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
849			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
850			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
851				continue
852			}
853			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
854			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
855			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
856			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
857				segs[0] != "" &&
858				segs[1] == "documents" &&
859				segs[2] != "" &&
860				segs[3] == "changes" {
861				return false
862			}
863			return true
864		}
865		return false
866	}

868	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
869	// namespace but is not at one of its six exact locations:
870	//
871	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
872	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
873	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/compact
874	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/query
875	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/list
876	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
877	//
878	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"compact"/"query"/"list"/"subscribe" segment, an extra
879	// segment, or a "crdt" segment in the keyword position (immediately past the
880	// document identifier) short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would
881	// answer those with a plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints
882	// must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the
883	// guard itself.
884	//
885	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
886	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
887	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
888	// keeps its ordinary routes. Likewise "compact", "query" and "list" are
889	// endpoint keywords only in the fifth segment; a session or document literally
890	// named any of them is an ordinary identifier.
891	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
892		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
893		if !ok {
894			return false
895		}
896		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
897		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
898			return false
899		}
900		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit, the state read, the
901		// compaction, the batch lookup and the ordered listing are all exactly
902		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state,compact,query,list};
903		// the subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
904		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
905			segs[0] != "" &&
906			segs[2] != "" &&
907			segs[4] == "ops"
908		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
909			segs[0] != "" &&
910			segs[2] != "" &&
911			segs[4] == "state"
912		validCompact := len(segs) == 5 &&
913			segs[0] != "" &&
914			segs[2] != "" &&
915			segs[4] == "compact"
916		validQuery := len(segs) == 5 &&
917			segs[0] != "" &&
918			segs[2] != "" &&
919			segs[4] == "query"
920		validList := len(segs) == 5 &&
921			segs[0] != "" &&
922			segs[2] != "" &&
923			segs[4] == "list"
924		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
925			segs[0] != "" &&
926			segs[2] != "" &&
927			segs[4] == "state" &&
928			segs[5] == "subscribe"
929		return !(validOps || validState || validCompact || validQuery || validList || validSubscribe)
930	}

942	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
943	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
944	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
945	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
946	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
947	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
948	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
949		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
950		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
951			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
952			return false
953		}
954	
955		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
956		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
957		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
958			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
959			return false
960		}
961		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
962		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
963			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
964			return false
965		}
966		return true
967	}

1381	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
1382	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.

1390			}
1391		}

1399	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1400	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1401		var n int64
1402		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1403			return 0, false
1404		}

1406		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1407		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1408		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1409			return 0, false
1410		}
1411		for _, c := range trimmed {
1412			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1413				return 0, false
1414			}
1415		}
1416		return n, true
1417	}

1425		}

396	// handleSetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes a registered device's read
397	// access to one attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
398	// unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write; repeating the current
399	// state is idempotent (changed=false). Only the creator may change access: a
400	// non-creator caller gets a 403 and an unknown attachment a 404, neither
401	// touching any access state. A rejected request (bad content type, malformed
402	// JSON, trailing content, empty or mistyped fields, unknown action) is a 400
403	// JSON error and writes nothing; an unregistered target device is a 404 JSON
404	// error. A granted device reads the same metadata and chunk bytes as the
405	// creator; a revoke returns its reads to 403 at once and never deletes
406	// stored chunks or sealed content.
407	func handleSetAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
408		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
409		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
410	
411		var req permissionRequest
412		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
413			return
414		}
415		if req.DeviceID == "" {
416			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
417			return
418		}
419		var authorized bool
420		switch req.Action {
421		case "grant":
422			authorized = true
423		case "revoke":
424			authorized = false
425		default:
426			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `action must be "grant" or "revoke"`)
427			return
428		}
429	
430		changed, err := s.SetAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, req.DeviceID, authorized)
431		if err != nil {
432			switch {
433			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
434				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
435			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
436				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
437			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
438				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
439			default:
440				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to update attachment access")
441			}
442			return
443		}
444	
445		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
446			"deviceId":   req.DeviceID,
447			"authorized": authorized,
448			"changed":    changed,
449		})
450	}
451	
452	// handleDeleteAttachment removes an upload outright. Only the creating device
453	// may delete: any other device gets a 403 and an unknown (or already deleted)
454	// id a 404, neither writing anything. A successful delete answers the
455	// attachment id and a deletion marker, after which the record, its chunks,
456	// its completion state and every access grant are gone: every later read,
457	// chunk write, finish or access change against the id is a 404, and
458	// re-creating the id starts a brand-new upload. Digest-addressed content is
459	// reclaimed only when no finished attachment references it any longer.
460	func handleDeleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
461		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
462		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
463	
464		if err := s.DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID); err != nil {
465			switch {
466			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
467				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
468			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
469				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
470			default:
471				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to delete attachment")
472			}
473			return
474		}
475	
476		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": attachmentID, "deleted": true})
477	}
478	
479	// isLowerHexSHA256 reports whether s is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
480	func isLowerHexSHA256(s string) bool {
481		if len(s) != 64 {
482			return false
483		}
484		for _, c := range s {
485			if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
486				return false
487			}
488		}
489		return true
490	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
84		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
85	
86		return &App{
87			Store:    kernel,
88			events:   eventService,
89			crdt:     crdtService,
90			Authz:    permissions,
91			pushSubs: push.NewRegistry(),
92		}, nil
93	}
94	
95	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
96	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
97	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
98	
99	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
100		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
101	}
102	
103	// Events returns the change event service.
104	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
105	
106	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
107	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
108	
109	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
110	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
111	
112	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
113	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
114	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
115	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
116	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
117		a.events.InterruptWaits()
118		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
119	}
120	
121	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
122	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
123		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
124	}
125	
126	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
127	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
128	func (a *App) Close() error {
129		a.events.InterruptWaits()
130		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
131		a.events.WaitDrained()
132		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
133		return a.Store.Close()
134	}
135	
136	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
137	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
138		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
139	}
140	
141	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
142	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
143		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
144	}
145	
146	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
147	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
148	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
149	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
150	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
151		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
152	}
153	
154	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
155	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart
156	// to ReplayChanges and commits through the same gated transaction the
157	// session-scoped batch commit uses, so the two paths cannot drift.
158	func (a *App) ReplaySessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
159		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
160	}
161	
162	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
163	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
164		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
165	}
166	
167	// MergeSessionChange merges a single change whose device identity was resolved
168	// from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
169	// gated merge: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
170	// serialized transaction as the merge judgment and append, so a revoked device
171	// writes nothing and a rejected request observes no change content.
172	func (a *App) MergeSessionChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
173		return a.events.MergeChangeAuthorized(documentID, baseCursor, c)
174	}
175	
176	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
177	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
178		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
179	}
180	
181	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
182	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
183		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
184	}
185	
186	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
187	// interval has no upper bound.
188	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
189		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
190	}
191	
192	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
193	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
194		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
195	}

197	// RestoreSessionSnapshot restores a snapshot as an ordinary change whose
198	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to
199	// the change event service's gated restore: the registration/permission
200	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the snapshot
201	// lookup and the append, so a revoked device writes nothing and a rejected
202	// request observes no snapshot or change content.
203	func (a *App) RestoreSessionSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
204		return a.events.RestoreSnapshotAuthorized(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
205	}

207	// PutSnapshotVersion binds an existing snapshot cursor to a stable version
208	// name, delegating to the change event service's gated transaction: the
209	// registration/permission verdict is taken before the snapshot and version
210	// are observed, so a rejected request exposes neither.
211	func (a *App) PutSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string, cursor int64) (events.VersionResult, error) {
212		return a.events.PutSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name, cursor)
213	}

215	// ListSnapshotVersions delegates to the change event service.
216	func (a *App) ListSnapshotVersions(documentID, deviceID string) ([]events.SnapshotVersion, error) {
217		return a.events.ListSnapshotVersions(documentID, deviceID)
218	}
219	
220	// GetSnapshotVersionState delegates to the change event service, resolving a
221	// version name to its snapshot cursor and stored state.
222	func (a *App) GetSnapshotVersionState(documentID, deviceID, name string) (int64, json.RawMessage, error) {
223		return a.events.GetSnapshotVersionState(documentID, deviceID, name)
224	}

226	// RebindSnapshotVersion moves a version name onto another existing snapshot,
227	// delegating to the change event service's gated transaction.
228	func (a *App) RebindSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string, cursor int64) (events.VersionResult, error) {
229		return a.events.RebindSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name, cursor)
230	}

232	// DeleteSnapshotVersion hard-deletes one version marker, delegating to the
233	// change event service's gated transaction; the snapshot itself is untouched.
234	func (a *App) DeleteSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string) error {
235		return a.events.DeleteSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name)
236	}

238	// RestoreSnapshotVersion restores the snapshot a version name points at as an
239	// ordinary change, delegating to the change event service's gated restore.
240	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, changeID, name string) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
241		return a.events.RestoreSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, changeID, name)
242	}

244	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
245	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
246		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
247	}

250	// interval has no upper bound.
251	func (a *App) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ListedChange, error) {
252		return a.events.ExportChanges(documentID, from, to)
253	}

255	// GetChangesByIDs delegates to the change event service's read-only batch
256	// lookup: per-id found/compacted/missing answers in request order, gated on
257	// the calling device's registration and document permission.
258	func (a *App) GetChangesByIDs(documentID, deviceID string, ids []string) ([]events.ChangeLookup, error) {
259		return a.events.GetChangesByIDs(documentID, deviceID, ids)
260	}

262	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
263	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
264		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
265	}
266	
267	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
268	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
269		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
270	}
271	
272	// CompactChanges delegates to the change event service.
273	func (a *App) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
274		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
275	}
276	
277	// CompactSessionChanges compacts a document's change log for a caller whose
278	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to
279	// the change event service's gated compaction: the registration/permission
280	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the trim, so a
281	// revoked device removes nothing and a rejected request observes no change
282	// content. It is the session counterpart to CompactChanges; the boundary,
283	// retained summaries and persistence semantics are identical.
284	func (a *App) CompactSessionChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
285		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
286	}
287	
288	// AddSubscription delegates to the change event service.
289	func (a *App) AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (wakes <-chan struct{}, revoked <-chan struct{}, deleted <-chan struct{}, unregister func()) {
290		return a.events.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
291	}
292	
293	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
294	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
295	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
296	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
297	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
298	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
299	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
300	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
301	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
302	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
303	//
304	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
305	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
306	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
307	// immediately, stickily.
308	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
309		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
310		if err != nil {
311			return err
312		}
313		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
314	
315		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
316			return err
317		}
318		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
319			return err
320		}
321		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
322			return err
323		}
324	
325		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
326		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
327		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
328		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
329		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
330		return nil
331	}
332	
333	// ---- Document-level deletion. ----
334	
335	// DeleteDocument removes a registered device's whole document in one
336	// serialized, synchronously committed transaction. The calling device is
337	// declared by deviceId — no new authentication is introduced.
338	//
339	// The fixed verdict order is taken inside the transaction, before any cleanup:
340	//
341	//   - an unregistered device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and writes
342	//     nothing;
343	//   - a device whose permission for the document was revoked yields
344	//     store.ErrPermissionDenied (403) and no cleanup runs;
345	//   - a document with no durable data anywhere — never created or already
346	//     deleted — yields events.ErrDocumentNotFound (404) and writes nothing.
347	//
348	// On success every row of the document is removed as one judgment: its online
349	// and trimmed change log, the retained idempotency summaries, its snapshots
350	// and named snapshot-version markers, its CRDT state and the per-document
351	// permission ledger. The same id is a brand-new document afterward — the
352	// cursor space restarts at 1 — and inherits no history or version names.
353	// Concurrent deletes commit at most once because the existence verdict and
354	// the deletions share one immediate transaction on the single connection.
355	//
356	// Only after the commit is durable are the document's live subscriptions
357	// ended (close code 4420 on both push channels) and dropped from the
358	// management registry; other documents' and devices' connections are
359	// untouched.
360	func (a *App) DeleteDocument(documentID, deviceID string) error {
361		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
362		if err != nil {
363			return err
364		}
365		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
366	
367		// Registration first, then permission, both before any document content
368		// is observed: a rejected delete reveals nothing and cleans nothing.
369		if err := a.Authz.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
370			return err
371		}
372	
373		eventsExist, err := a.events.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
374		if err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		crdtExist, err := a.crdt.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
378		if err != nil {
379			return err
380		}
381		// A ledger-only deviation row also counts as document data, so a document
382		// whose only durable trace is a grant/revoke still deletes cleanly and the
383		// re-created id inherits no authorization state.
384		ledgerExist, err := a.Authz.DocumentHasRowsTx(tx, documentID)
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		if !eventsExist && !crdtExist && !ledgerExist {
389			return events.ErrDocumentNotFound
390		}
391	
392		if err := a.events.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
393			return err
394		}
395		if err := a.crdt.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
396			return err
397		}
398		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
399			return err
400		}
401	
402		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
403			return err
404		}
405	
406		// End the document's live subscriptions on both channels and drop them
407		// from the management registry only after the cleanup is durable: the
408		// close is one-shot per connection, so a client re-subscribing to the
409		// now-fresh id opens a new connection and never reopens the ended ones.
410		a.events.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
411		a.crdt.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
412		a.CloseDocumentPush(documentID)
413		return nil
414	}
415	
416	// ---- Permission service boundary. ----
417	
418	// SetDocumentPermission delegates to the permission service.
419	func (a *App) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (bool, error) {
420		return a.Authz.SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID, authorized)
421	}
422	
423	// DocumentAuthorized delegates to the permission service.
424	func (a *App) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
425		return a.Authz.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
426	}
427	
428	// ListDocumentPermissions delegates to the permission service.
429	func (a *App) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]authz.PermissionEntry, error) {
430		return a.Authz.ListDocumentPermissions(documentID, limit, offset)
431	}
432	
433	// ---- CRDT state service boundary. ----
434	
435	// SubmitCRDTOps delegates to the CRDT state service.
436	func (a *App) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []crdt.Op) ([]crdt.Result, error) {
437		return a.crdt.SubmitOps(documentID, declaredType, ops)
438	}
439	
440	// GetCRDTState delegates to the CRDT state service.

451	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating
452	// to the CRDT state service's gated compaction: the registration/permission
453	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the trim, so a
454	// revoked device trims nothing and a rejected request observes no state
455	// content. It is the session counterpart to CompactCRDT; the trimming,
456	// retained identities, snapshot body and persistence semantics are
457	// identical.

1	// Package store is the durable kernel shared by the internal services: it
2	// owns the SQLite database handle and the registration layer (devices and
3	// sessions) plus resumable attachments.
4	//
5	// The business services layered on top of the kernel — the change event log,
6	// the permission ledger and the CRDT state — live in their own packages and
7	// cooperate only through their internal interfaces. They all share this one
8	// handle: it opens a single pooled connection with immediate write
9	// transactions, so every service's transactional judgment is serialized on
10	// the same connection and no batch is ever half written.
11	//
12	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer. A device registers with a
13	// client-supplied id; a session belongs to exactly one registered device and
14	// is addressed by its own client-supplied id. Registration and session
15	// creation are idempotent re-posts: the first call creates, an identical
16	// repeat does not. A session id already owned by another device is a
17	// conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are owner-scoped and hard: a
18	// repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device path all miss with 404,
19	// after which the id is free to be created again. A device itself can
20	// deregister: the device row and everything it owns — its sessions and the
21	// attachments it created, chunks and grants included — vanish in one
22	// serialized transaction, a repeat or never-registered deregistration misses
23	// with 404 and writes nothing, and the freed id registers again as a
24	// brand-new device.
25	//
26	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
27	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
28	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
29	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
30	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
31	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
32	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
33	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
34	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them. The creator may grant
35	// other registered devices read-only access per attachment; every
36	// (attachment, device) pair starts unauthorized, grants and revokes commit in
37	// the same serialized way, and access never widens the write paths. Deletes
38	// are owner-scoped and hard: the record, its chunks and its grants vanish in
39	// one serialized transaction, a repeat delete misses with 404, the id is free
40	// to be created again, and the shared content bytes are reclaimed once the
41	// last completed attachment referencing them is gone.
42	package store
43	
44	import (
45		"database/sql"
46		"encoding/json"
47		"errors"
48		"fmt"
49	
50		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
51	)
52	
53	// ErrDeviceNotFound reports that an operation targets a device id that was
54	// never registered. Services map it to 404; nothing is written.
55	var ErrDeviceNotFound = errors.New("device not found")
56	
57	// ErrPermissionDenied reports that a device's access to a document has been
58	// revoked. Services map it to 403; nothing is written and no document content
59	// is exposed. It is a shared verdict produced by the permission service and
60	// consulted by every service that enforces the gate inside a transaction.
61	var ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("device permission for this document has been revoked")
62	
63	// ErrSessionConflict reports that a session id already belongs to a different
64	// device. The session keeps its original owner; nothing is written. Services
65	// map it to 409.
66	type ErrSessionConflict struct {
67		ID string
68	}
69	
70	func (e *ErrSessionConflict) Error() string {
71		return fmt.Sprintf("session %q belongs to another device", e.ID)
72	}
73	
74	// ErrSessionNotFound reports that no live session matches the (device,
75	// session) pair: the session was never created, was already deleted, or
76	// belongs to another device. Services map it to 404.
77	var ErrSessionNotFound = errors.New("session not found")
78	
79	// DBTX is the subset of *sql.DB and *sql.Tx the services use for their
80	// serialized work, so judgments made "in the same transaction" (for example a
81	// permission gate followed by the gated write) run on one concrete connection
82	// whether the caller holds a transaction or the handle itself.
83	type DBTX interface {
84		Exec(query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error)
85		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
86		QueryRow(query string, args ...any) *sql.Row
87	}
88	
89	// Store is the durable kernel: one SQLite database handle together with the
90	// device, session and attachment data it owns.
91	type Store struct {
92		db *sql.DB
93	}
94	
95	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
96	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
97	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
98		if path == "" {
99			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
100			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
101			path = "file::memory:"
102		}
103		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
104		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
105		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
111		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
112		// for readers does not help correctness here. It also keeps every
113		// service's transaction serialized on the same connection.
114		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
115		s := &Store{db: db}
116		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
117			_ = db.Close()
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		return s, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DB returns the underlying handle. The business services use it to open the
124	// serialized transactions their judgments run in; callers outside the
125	// internal packages never need it.
126	func (s *Store) DB() *sql.DB { return s.db }
127	
128	// Close releases the database handle.
129	func (s *Store) Close() error {
130		return s.db.Close()
131	}
132	
133	func (s *Store) init() error {
134		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
135	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (
136		id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
137	);
138	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
139		id        TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
140		device_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id)
141	);
142	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_device_idx
143		ON sessions(device_id);
144	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachments (
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id),
147		total_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
148		chunk_size  INTEGER NOT NULL,
149		sha256      TEXT NOT NULL,
150		complete    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
151		reused      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
152		created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
153	);
154	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_chunks (
155		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
156		idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
157		data          BLOB NOT NULL,
158		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, idx)
159	);
160	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_contents (
161		sha256 TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
162		size   INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		data   BLOB NOT NULL
164	);
165	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_access (
166		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
167		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
168		authorized    INTEGER NOT NULL,
169		granted_seq   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
170		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
171	);
172	`)
173		if err != nil {
174			return err
175		}
176		if err := s.ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq(); err != nil {
177			return err
178		}
179		return s.ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq()
180	}
181	
182	// ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq adds the creation-order column to databases
183	// created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled in insertion
184	// (rowid) order so their relative listing order is unchanged; new rows take
185	// strictly larger values, so the sequence never reuses a value even after
186	// the newest attachment is deleted and its id created again.
187	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq() error {
188		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachments)`)
189		if err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		hasColumn := false
193		for rows.Next() {
194			var cid, notNull, pk int
195			var name, colType string
196			var dflt sql.NullString
197			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
198				_ = rows.Close()
199				return err
200			}
201			if name == "created_seq" {
202				hasColumn = true
203			}
204		}
205		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
206			_ = rows.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209		_ = rows.Close()
210		if hasColumn {
211			return nil
212		}
213		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
214			`ALTER TABLE attachments ADD COLUMN created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
215		); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		_, err = s.db.Exec(
219			`UPDATE attachments SET created_seq = (
220				SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attachments older WHERE older.rowid <= attachments.rowid
221			)`,
222		)
223		return err
224	}
225	
226	// ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq adds the grant-order column to access
227	// tables created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled one past the
228	// per-attachment maximum in insertion (rowid) order, so surviving grants keep
229	// a stable relative order; every new grant takes a strictly larger value, even
230	// after the previously newest grant was revoked, so a re-granted device lists
231	// at the position of its latest grant and a value is never reused.
232	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq() error {
233		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachment_access)`)
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		hasColumn := false
238		for rows.Next() {
239			var cid, notNull, pk int
240			var name, colType string
241			var dflt sql.NullString
242			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
243				_ = rows.Close()
244				return err
245			}
246			if name == "granted_seq" {
247				hasColumn = true
248			}
249		}
250		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251			_ = rows.Close()
252			return err
253		}
254		_ = rows.Close()
255		if hasColumn {
256			return nil
257		}
258		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
259			`ALTER TABLE attachment_access ADD COLUMN granted_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
260		); err != nil {
261			return err
262		}
263		_, err = s.db.Exec(
264			`UPDATE attachment_access SET granted_seq = (
265				SELECT rn FROM (
266					SELECT rowid AS rid,
267					       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY attachment_id ORDER BY rowid) AS rn
268					FROM attachment_access
269				) WHERE rid = attachment_access.rowid
270			)`,
271		)
272		return err
273	}
274	
275	// RegisterDevice registers a device by client-supplied id. The first call for
276	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
277	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.
278	func (s *Store) RegisterDevice(deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
279		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
280		if err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
284	
285		created, err = RegisterDeviceTx(tx, deviceID)
286		if err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return created, tx.Commit()
290	}
291	
292	// RegisterDeviceTx is RegisterDevice against an existing transaction, so the
293	// services can resolve the registration layer as the first step of a larger
294	// serialized transaction (their permission/content gates then share it).
295	func RegisterDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
296		var exists bool
297		if err := q.QueryRow(
298			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
299		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
300			return false, err
301		}
302		if !exists {
303			if _, err := q.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
304				return false, err
305			}
306			return true, nil
307		}
308		return false, nil
309	}
310	
311	// DeviceExistsTx reports whether deviceID is registered, evaluated inside q so
312	// a service's gate runs on the same transaction as the work it guards.
313	func DeviceExistsTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
314		var exists bool
315		if err := q.QueryRow(
316			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
317		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
318			return false, err
319		}
320		return exists, nil
321	}
322	
323	// CreateSession creates a session owned by deviceID with a client-supplied id.
324	//
325	//   - An unknown device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
326	//   - A session id already owned by another device yields *ErrSessionConflict;
327	//     nothing is written and the owner is unchanged.
328	//   - Re-posting the same (device, session) pair is idempotent: created=false.
329	//
330	// A deleted session is gone for good, so its id can be registered again as a
331	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
332	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
333	// cannot both create it.
334	func (s *Store) CreateSession(deviceID, sessionID string) (created bool, err error) {
335		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
336		if err != nil {
337			return false, err
338		}
339		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
340	
341		var deviceExists bool
342		if err := tx.QueryRow(
343			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
344		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
345			return false, err
346		}
347		if !deviceExists {
348			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
349		}
350	
351		var owner string
352		err = tx.QueryRow(
353			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
354		).Scan(&owner)
355		switch {
356		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
357			if _, err := tx.Exec(
358				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
359				sessionID, deviceID,
360			); err != nil {
361				return false, err
362			}
363			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
364				return false, err
365			}
366			return true, nil
367		case err != nil:
368			return false, err
369		}
370	
371		if owner != deviceID {
372			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}
373		}
374		return false, tx.Commit()
375	}
376	
377	// DeleteSession removes the live session matching the (deviceID, sessionID)
378	// pair. Any miss — the session does not exist, was already deleted, or belongs
379	// to another device — returns ErrSessionNotFound and changes nothing. The
380	// check and the delete run in one transaction, so a concurrent create cannot
381	// interleave and a repeat delete still misses; the removal is committed to
382	// disk before the call returns.
383	func (s *Store) DeleteSession(deviceID, sessionID string) error {
384		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
389	
390		var owner string
391		err = tx.QueryRow(
392			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
393		).Scan(&owner)
394		switch {
395		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
396			return ErrSessionNotFound
397		case err != nil:
398			return err
399		}
400		if owner != deviceID {
401			return ErrSessionNotFound
402		}
403	
404		if _, err := tx.Exec(
405			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
406			sessionID, deviceID,
407		); err != nil {
408			return err
409		}
410		return tx.Commit()
411	}
412	
413	// DeleteDeviceTx deregisters deviceID and removes every record it owns, all
414	// inside the caller's serialized transaction:
415	//
416	//   - the device's sessions are hard-deleted, so their session-scoped reads
417	//     and subscriptions miss from then on;
418	//   - every attachment it created is removed together with its chunks, its
419	//     sealed/unfinished state and the access rows other devices held on it;
420	//   - the read grants the device itself held on other devices' attachments
421	//     are withdrawn;
422	//   - the device row is removed last (every child row goes first).
423	//
424	// Digest-addressed content is shared across attachments and is reclaimed only
425	// when no completed attachment still references a digest — exactly the rule
426	// of a single attachment delete — so another device's attachment with the same
427	// digest keeps its bytes and one deregistration by itself never reclaims
428	// shared content. The document permission ledger lives in the authz package
429	// and clears its own rows against the same transaction through
430	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx.
431	//
432	// An unknown (never registered or already deregistered) device yields
433	// ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing. Because the whole judgment runs in one
434	// immediate transaction on the single shared connection, concurrent
435	// deregistrations of the same device commit at most once and any concurrent
436	// chunk upload or finish either committed entirely before it or is rejected
437	// entirely afterward — no half-written record survives.
438	func DeleteDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) error {
439		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
440		if err != nil {
441			return err
442		}
443		if !exists {
444			return ErrDeviceNotFound
445		}
446	
447		// Remember the digests of the device's completed attachments before their
448		// rows vanish: each is a candidate for content reclamation once every
449		// owned attachment is gone. DISTINCT because several of the device's
450		// attachments may share the same digest-addressed content.
451		rows, err := q.Query(
452			`SELECT DISTINCT sha256 FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ? AND complete = 1`,
453			deviceID,
454		)
455		if err != nil {
456			return err
457		}
458		var digests []string
459		for rows.Next() {
460			var digest string
461			if err := rows.Scan(&digest); err != nil {
462				_ = rows.Close()
463				return err
464			}
465			digests = append(digests, digest)
466		}
467		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
468			_ = rows.Close()
469			return err
470		}
471		if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
472			return err
473		}
474	
475		// Withdraw the read grants this device held on other devices'
476		// attachments (rows naming it as the grantee), then remove the access
477		// rosters of the attachments it created before the attachment rows those
478		// rosters reference are deleted.
479		if _, err := q.Exec(
480			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
481		); err != nil {
482			return err
483		}
484		if _, err := q.Exec(
485			`DELETE FROM attachment_access
486			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
487			deviceID,
488		); err != nil {
489			return err
490		}
491		if _, err := q.Exec(
492			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks
493			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
494			deviceID,
495		); err != nil {
496			return err
497		}
498		if _, err := q.Exec(
499			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
500		); err != nil {
501			return err
502		}
503	
504		// Reclaim each digest-addressed content only when no surviving completed
505		// attachment — owned by another device, or by the deregistered device in
506		// an impossible re-read — still references it.

1900	func handlePollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1901		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1902	
1903		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1904		if !ok {
1905			return
1906		}
1907		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1908		if !ok {
1909			return
1910		}
1911	
1912		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1913			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1914		)
1915		switch {
1916		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1917			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1918			return
1919		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1920			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1921			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1922			return
1923		case err != nil:
1924			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1925			return
1926		}
1927	
1928		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1929	}

1931	// handleSessionPollChanges is the session-scoped long-poll continuation over
1932	// the same change collection the session reads page:
1933	//
1934	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/poll
1935	//
1936	// The request is a GET with no body; the calling device is the session's
1937	// owning device resolved with the same identity rule as the session reads,
1938	// exports, commits and subscriptions. Query parameters and the success body are
1939	// identical to GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/changes/poll — after (default 0),
1940	// limit (default 100, 1..1000) and waitMs (default 0, 0..30000), answered with
1941	// changes, nextCursor and timedOut in that order, rows ascending by cursor.
1942	//
1943	// Rows already past after return immediately with timedOut=false; a known
1944	// document caught up to after parks until the first commit through any write
1945	// path (session batch commit, document commit, merge, restore, replay) or the
1946	// wait deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at
1947	// once and never parks. A deadline expiry returns the empty page, echoes the
1948	// caller's after and sets timedOut=true without advancing the cursor. Checks
1949	// run in the fixed order request shape and parameters (400), session
1950	// existence (404), document permission (403); a rejected request exposes no
1951	// change content. A client disconnect simply cancels the wait and writes
1952	// nothing; while the service is shutting down the parked request answers a
1953	// JSON 503.
1954	func handleSessionPollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1955		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1956		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1957	
1958		// Parameter shape precedes the session lookup, matching the session paged
1959		// read's ordering: a malformed after/limit/waitMs against an unknown
1960		// session is still a 400.
1961		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1962		if !ok {
1963			return
1964		}
1965		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1966		if !ok {
1967			return
1968		}
1969	
1970		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1971		if err != nil {
1972			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1973				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1974				return
1975			}
1976			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1977			return
1978		}
1979	
1980		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
1981		if err != nil {
1982			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
1983			return
1984		}
1985		if !authorized {
1986			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1987			return
1988		}
1989	
1990		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1991			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1992		)
1993		switch {
1994		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1995			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1996			return
1997		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1998			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1999			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
2000			return
2001		case err != nil:
2002			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
2003			return
2004		}
2005	
2006		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
2007	}
2008	
2009	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
2010	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
2011	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
2012	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
2013	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
2014	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
2015	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
2016	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
2017	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
2018		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
2019	
2020		var req replayRequest
2021		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
2022			return
2023		}
2024		if req.DeviceID == "" {
2025			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
2026			return
2027		}
2028		if req.Operations == nil {
2029			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
2030			return
2031		}
2032		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
2033			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
2034			return
2035		}
2036	
2037		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
2038		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
2039		for i, op := range req.Operations {
2040			if op.ID == "" {
2041				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
2042				return
2043			}
2044			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
2045				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
2046				return
2047			}
2048			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
2049				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
2050				return
2051			}
2052			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
2053			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
2054		}
2055	
2056		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
2057		if err != nil {
2058			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
2059			switch {
2060			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
2061				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
2062			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
2063				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
2064			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
2065				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
2066					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
2067					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
2068				})
2069			default:
2070				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
2071			}
2072			return
2073		}
2074	
2075		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
2076	}

40	数据库成功打开且监听建立后返回 `200` `{"status":"ok"}`。监听尚未建立或数据库初始化失败（即启动未完成）时不宣称就绪：此时整个服务表面（含 `/healthz` 自身）返回 `503` JSON 错误（`{"error":"service is not ready"}`），健康检查不会得到成功响应，业务接口也不可达；就绪后设备、会话、权限、文档与附件接口才在实际监听地址上提供服务，且 `/healthz` 的 `200` 状态码与 JSON 形状不变。
41	
42	### `POST /v1/devices`
43	
44	注册设备。仅接受 `Content-Type: application/json`。请求体：
45	
46	```json
47	{"deviceId": "device-1"}
48	```
49	
50	- `deviceId` 为非空字符串；类型头不符、JSON 非法、尾随内容、缺失或类型错误（数字、布尔、`null` 等）均返回 `400` JSON 错误且零写入。
51	- 首次注册返回 `200` `{"deviceId":"device-1","created":true}`；用同一 `deviceId` 重试是幂等的，返回 `200` `created=false`。
52	
53	### `DELETE /v1/devices/{deviceId}`
54	
55	注销设备，让停用或遗失的设备把自己和名下数据一次性清掉。无请求体，路径上的 `deviceId` 就是调用者身份。
56	
57	- 成功返回一行 JSON：`200` `{"deviceId":"device-1","deleted":true}`，不新增其他字段。
58	- 设备从未注册，或重复注销，一律返回 `404` JSON 错误且零写入；并发注销同一设备时至多一次真正生效。
59	- 路径标识为空（连续斜杠或尾随斜杠）、路径段缺失或多余、方法不匹配均返回 `400` JSON 错误，不重定向也不输出 HTML。
60	- 注销在一个序列化事务内完成并同步落盘：
61	  - 该设备名下的会话全部硬删除，此后这些会话的增量读取与订阅返回 `404` JSON；权限撤回的既有 `403` 判定顺序不变。
62	  - 它创建的附件连同分块、封存状态和未完成上传一起删除，任何人再读（元数据、分块、访问名单）一律 `404`；注销期间并发进行的分块上传与封存要么整体完成要么整体拒绝，不留下半截记录。
63	  - 它对他人附件的读取授权被撤回（他人附件的授权名单不再出现它），他人授予它的读取资格一并失效（它的附件清单不再出现他人附件）。
64	  - 文档权限台账中该设备的授权一并清除；同摘要内容的去重字节只在最后一个引用消失时回收，单次注销不影响其他设备附件的复用与读取。
65	  - 不删除其他设备的变更记录、快照与文档内容，这些读取结果照旧；其他设备的变更读取、合并与恢复语义不变。
66	- 它的订阅连接（增量订阅与 CRDT 状态订阅）在提交后立即以 `4403` 关闭；重连时支撑连接的会话已不存在，在升级前返回 `404`。
67	- 注销后同名 `deviceId` 可以重新注册，按全新设备处理，不继承任何会话、权限或附件。
68	- 进程重启后注销结果保持一致，重复注销依旧返回 `404` 且零写入。
69	
70	### `POST /v1/devices/{deviceId}/sessions`
71	
72	为已注册设备创建同步会话。仅接受 `Content-Type: application/json`。请求体：
73	
74	```json
75	{"sessionId": "session-1"}
76	```
77	
78	- `sessionId` 为非空字符串；类型头不符、JSON 非法、尾随内容、缺失或类型错误均返回 `400` JSON 错误且零写入。
79	- 设备未注册返回 `404` JSON 错误且零写入。
80	- 首次创建返回 `200` `{"sessionId":"session-1","created":true}`；同一设备用同一 `sessionId` 重试幂等返回 `created=false`。
81	- `sessionId` 已归属其他设备时返回 `409` JSON 错误且零写入，归属永不改变。
82	- 创建在序列化事务内完成；并发创建同一 `sessionId` 恰好一个成功，其余同设备幂等、异设备 `409`。
83	
84	### `DELETE /v1/devices/{deviceId}/sessions/{sessionId}`
85	
86	仅删除该设备名下匹配的会话，无请求体。
87	
88	- 命中返回 `200` `{"deleted":true}`。
89	- 设备不存在、会话不存在、会话归属其他设备、或重复删除，一律返回 `404` JSON 错误；非属主的删除不会移除会话。
90	- 删除为硬删除并同步落盘；删除后该 `sessionId` 可作为全新会话再次创建（`created=true`），重启后重复删除仍为 `404`。
91	
92	### `GET /v1/devices/{deviceId}/subscriptions`
93	
94	设备的订阅管理只读入口：列出该设备当前**活着**的全部推送订阅连接。路径上的 `deviceId` 就是调用者唯一身份，不新增任何认证机制；无请求体。
95	
96	- 该设备经文档级订阅声明（查询参数 `deviceId`）建立的连接，以及经它名下会话建立的连接，都出现在列表里；增量变更订阅与 CRDT 状态订阅两种通道一并列出。
97	- 正文是一行紧凑 JSON 加末尾换行，顶层键按 `subscriptions`、`count` 的顺序固定出现：
98	
99	  ```json
100	  {"subscriptions":[{"subscriptionId":"sub-1","documentId":"doc-a","kind":"changes","cursor":5,"establishedAt":1727000000000}],"count":1}
101	  ```
102	
103	- 每条订阅固定给出五个字段且键序固定：`subscriptionId`（订阅标识，连接建立时由服务端分配，本进程内不重复，断开后不再出现于任何列表）、`documentId`（文档标识）、`kind`（通道种类：变更订阅为 `"changes"`，状态订阅为 `"state"`）、`cursor`（握手时请求的起始游标；状态订阅没有游标，这一项记 `0`）、`establishedAt`（连接建立时间，Unix 毫秒整数）。
104	- 全部条目按连接建立的先后升序排列，`count` 与数组长度始终一致。
105	- 列表是纯内存视图：客户端断开或进程重启后条目立即消失，不落盘、不写入任何记录，也不占用变更游标。没有任何存活订阅时照样返回 `200`，正文为 `{"subscriptions":[],"count":0}` 加换行——空列表不是错误。
106	- 调用设备未注册返回 `404` JSON 错误；路径标识为空（连续斜杠或尾随斜杠）、段缺失或多余、方法不匹配一律返回 `400` JSON 错误，不重定向也不输出 HTML。
107	
108	### `DELETE /v1/devices/{deviceId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`
109	
110	设备的订阅主动回收入口：按订阅标识结束该设备名下指定的那一条存活连接。路径上的 `deviceId` 是唯一身份，无请求体。

62			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
63			return
64		}
65

67		entries := make([]subscriptionEntry, 0, len(infos))

73				Cursor:         info.Cursor,
74				EstablishedAt:  info.EstablishedAt,
75			})

78	}

81	//
82	//	DELETE /v1/devices/{deviceId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
83	//

92	// changes nothing; a failure writes nothing, never redirects and never emits

108		if !s.CancelPushSubscription(deviceID, subscriptionID) {

  ```

- 每条清单项只给出 `sessionId` 一个字段；同一会话在一次结果里最多出现一次，并按会话标识的字典序升序排列（与创建先后无关）。`count` 给出本页条数，始终与数组长度一致。

- 任一非法分页取值先于其他判定返回 `400` JSON 错误；设备未注册或已注销返回 `404` JSON 错误，且不返回任何清单内容。判定顺序固定为请求形状再到设备存在性，前序失败优先返回。

- 清单是只读动作：不创建或删除会话，也不占用变更游标或推送订阅。已删除的会话不再出现；设备注销时名下会话一并从清单消失，此后该设备的清单返回 `404`，重新注册同名设备时按全新设备返回空清单。

### `GET /v1/devices/{deviceId}/sessions`

设备的会话清单只读入口：让客户端断线重连后浏览它名下当前全部同步会话。挂在设备资源的会话集合路径上，用 `GET` 读取且不带请求体；路径上的设备标识就是调用者身份，不新增任何认证机制。

- 返回 `200`，正文是一行紧凑 JSON 加末尾换行，顶层键按会话数组与条数的顺序固定出现：

  ```
  {"sessions":[{"sessionId":"session-1"},{"sessionId":"session-2"}],"count":2}
  ```

- 每条清单项只给出 `sessionId` 一个字段；同一会话在一次结果里最多出现一次，并按会话标识的字典序升序排列（与创建先后无关）。`count` 给出本页条数，始终与数组长度一致。
- 分页在这一固定顺序上切片，参数口径与附件清单一致：`limit` 只接受 `1..1000` 的整数，缺省 `100`；`offset` 只接受非负整数，缺省 `0`，表示先跳过前面若干条。两次读取之间没有增删会话时，翻页得到的条目不重不漏；越过末尾时返回空数组与零计数（`{"sessions":[],"count":0}` 加换行），空清单不是错误。
- 任一非法分页取值先于其他判定返回 `400` JSON 错误；设备未注册或已注销返回 `404` JSON 错误，且不返回任何清单内容。判定顺序固定为请求形状再到设备存在性，前序失败优先返回。
- 标识为空（连续斜杠或尾随斜杠）、段缺失或多余、方法不匹配（`POST` 创建除外）一律返回 `400` JSON 错误，不重定向也不输出 HTML。取名 `sessions` 的设备标识按普通标识处理，`sessions` 这个词只在端点段位置才被识别为关键字。
- 清单是只读动作：不创建或删除会话，也不占用变更游标或推送订阅。已删除的会话不再出现；设备注销时名下会话一并从清单消失，此后该设备的清单返回 `404`，重新注册同名设备时按全新设备返回空清单。
- 重复请求与进程重启后，同一请求的正文逐字不变，读取不改动任何状态。本入口不改变会话创建、删除、订阅管理与附件清单等入口的既有语义。

content.text:
All three pieces are complete and the full suite (including `-race`) passes. Here's a summary.

## What was added

A new read-only endpoint **`GET /v1/devices/{deviceId}/sessions`** for browsing a device's sessions after reconnect.

**Store layer** — `internal/store/store.go`
- `ListSessions(deviceID, limit, offset)` returns the device's live session ids, each once, sorted lexicographically by `id ASC`, sliced with `LIMIT/OFFSET` in one serialized read transaction. Unregistered device → `ErrDeviceNotFound`; past-end offset → empty non-nil slice. Deleted sessions are absent and device deregistration already cascades its sessions away.

**HTTP layer** — `internal/server/sessions_list.go` + routes in `server.go`
- Body is one compact JSON line + newline with fixed key order: `{"sessions":[{"sessionId":"…"},…],"count":N}`; `count` is the page length; empty page is `{"sessions":[],"count":0}`.
- Pagination reuses the attachment listing's exact parser (`limit` 1–1000 default 100, `offset` ≥0 default 0); invalid params return **400 before** the device lookup; unregistered/deregistered device → **404** with no listing content.
- Routing: shares the collection path with `POST` (create); wrong verbs → JSON 400; a GET with extra segments → JSON 400. I made the extra-segment guard **GET-specific** deliberately so the pre-existing pinned behavior `DELETE …/sessions/s1/extra` → 404 stays intact. A device literally named `sessions` routes as an ordinary id (keyword recognized only in the endpoint segment).
- Read-only: no create/delete, no change cursor, no push subscription; bodies are byte-identical on repeat and across restart.

**Tests**
- `internal/store/sessions_list_test.go`: ordering/ownership, pagination, delete+recreate, deregister cascade, restart durability.
- `internal/server/sessions_list_test.go`: contract & single-key items, exact byte shape, pagination/bounds, 400-before-404 ordering, shape errors (no redirect/HTML), body ignored on GET, delete/deregister/re-register, `sessions`-as-id keyword handling, and repeat/restart byte stability.

**Docs** — new `### GET /v1/devices/{deviceId}/sessions` section in `README.md` in the existing Chinese style; startup/readiness and all other endpoint semantics untouched.

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `go test ./...` (plus `-race` on the touched packages) all pass. I did not commit since you didn't ask me to.
